title: Canteen
goal: Every player has met Taka and at least a taste of the wider trainee body, and Section Nine has been assigned -- no choice offered -- to storm drain clearance. Whether they know it's more than that by the time they leave depends entirely on what they asked.
howToPlay: Loud and warm for most of the scene, then one flat, deflating turn at the very end. This is the biggest room the six of them have been in together all day -- dozens of other trainees, established groups, a real sense of scale after a day of small, private moments. Let the social half breathe; then let the announcement land hard and end the scene on it. **Don't soften the assignment once it's read, and don't let anyone talk their way out of it.** That refusal is the whole point.

intro.where: The combined-campus canteen, first evening meal as a group. Dozens of other trainees already eating -- established tables, established jokes, a scale the six of them haven't been part of yet today.
intro.firstThing: Noise. A room built for four hundred people, most of the seats full, and Section Nine visibly the newest table in it.
intro.readAloud: The canteen is loud in the specific way a room gets when nobody in it has anywhere else to be. Long tables, most of them full, easy noise. You're new enough that it shows -- new kit, new faces, a table nobody's claimed yet.
intro.landmark: The long table nobody's claimed -- empty, obviously new, the one fixed point in a room that's otherwise all noise and motion.

carriesIn.when: Kit Issue was played first (it should be)
carriesIn.then: Whatever they picked is visibly unworn -- a small, funny tell next to trainees who've had theirs for months. Worth one line, not a whole beat.

intro.holdInReserve: One table near the door is laid for more people than are sitting at it, and nobody moves the spare chairs. Give this to anybody reading the room rather than joining it.

cast.label: Taka
cast.role: Older student, real Frame time, instant nicknames

brief.wants: To make six strangers feel like they already belong here, immediately, whether they're ready for it or not.
brief.opensWith: A nickname, delivered as already-decided fact, before anyone's introduced themselves.

willDiscuss.note: He has an opinion on everything and shares all of them. Genuinely warm, not performing it.
coercible below -- this is the only topic where the register actually changes.

willNotDiscuss.topic: Anything unkind about anybody, however openly he is invited to
willNotDiscuss.why: Not diplomacy and not caution -- it visibly costs him nothing to refuse, which is the most revealing thing about him. He will change the subject to something he likes instead, at volume.

coercible.topic: What's actually down in the storm drains
coercible.how: Ask him directly and specifically -- he won't volunteer it, but he won't lie if pushed.

voice.register: Exuberant, instantly familiar, total conviction. The nicknames arrive as settled fact, not an offer.
tics: Never asks permission for a nickname, just uses it and moves on
Talks at full volume regardless of what's being discussed
Goes quiet for exactly one beat when something real comes up, then deflects straight back to noise
samples: "Oh, you're -- " (already decided) " -- yeah, that's you now, don't fight it."
"First rule of the drill tomorrow: it will go wrong, it always goes wrong, that's why it's a drill."
"Storm drains, huh." (a beat, longer than anything else he says all night) "Wear the boots. Trust me."

cast.label: A pilot-track student, a table over
cast.role: Texture and contrast tonight -- GM-ONLY: a real, tracked recurring character. See data/npcs/the-young-one.json before running or editing him.

brief.wants: To mention, unprompted, that their own assignment is more interesting than whatever Section Nine gets.
brief.opensWith: Asking which track they're on before asking their names.

willDiscuss.note: Not unkind, just clearly convinced this matters more than anything Section Nine is about to be handed.

willNotDiscuss.topic: Anything that would suggest he is anything other than an ordinary, slightly competitive classmate
willNotDiscuss.why: GM-ONLY, load-bearing: he is Cicada Cadre and a Directorate Frame pilot (ideas/story/dossier-cicada.md #9). Nothing in this scene may hint at it, exactly the same discipline as Manako's first-meeting rule in episode-c1e1--the-errand.json. He does not know he is being watched for anything; he is just having dinner.

voice.register: Confident, a little competitive, not actually malicious.
tics: Turns most questions back to their own track
samples: "You're Section Nine? Rough. We got harbour patrol."

cast.label: A technical-track student, easier to talk to

brief.wants: An actual conversation, a rarer thing tonight than it should be.
brief.opensWith: Just asking how their first day went, genuinely.

willDiscuss.topic: What repair crew work is actually like
willDiscuss.note: Honest, a little tired, not glamorous and doesn't pretend otherwise.

willNotDiscuss.topic: Anything that would get another trainee in trouble
willNotDiscuss.why: Friendly about it and completely immovable. They will tell the party what a thing is; they will not tell them who did it.

voice.register: Quiet, warm, unhurried -- the easiest person in the room to end up next to.
tics: Asks a real follow-up question instead of talking about themselves
samples: "Nobody tells you how much of it is just... waiting for the part to actually break."

cast.label: The Section Officer
cast.role: Arrives near the end of the meal to read the assignments out himself

brief.wants: To watch Section Nine receive the worst job on the list, in person, from him.
brief.opensWith: Nothing to the party. He addresses the room, not them, and starts reading.

willDiscuss.note: Purely procedural. Access, time, kit. He will repeat it once, in the same tone, and not a third time.
"Sections are assigned work. That is what a section is." He does not elaborate and does not need to.

willNotDiscuss.why: Not handled in a canteen. Take it up through your section, which means take it up with him, later, and lose.

willNotDiscuss.topic: The errand, the vial, or this afternoon
willNotDiscuss.why: He has not mentioned it and will not. That conversation is Episode Two's opening scene.

voice.register: Clipped, procedural, faintly aggrieved. Reads a duty list the way other people read a shopping list.
tics: Calls them Section Nine, never by name
Answers a question by reading the relevant clause aloud
samples: "Section Nine: storm drain clearance, access via Dock C. Report by nineteen-hundred. Bring waders."
"Sections are assigned work. That is what a section is."
"Section Nine. -- Yes, you. Don't look round, there's only one of you."
"It's on the sheet. It's been on the sheet since this morning. Somebody should read the sheet."

beats.text: Establish scale before anything else happens -- this is the biggest room the six of them have shared all day, and most of the people in it are strangers.
beats.direction:
Let it feel different from every scene so far. Intake Medicals and Kit Issue were both small and administrative; this is loud, social, and for the first time today the six of them are visibly outnumbered by people who aren't them.

Somewhere under the noise, a radio nobody is really listening to: a man's voice, a phone-in programme, something about his daughter being held without charge. Nobody at the table has any reason to know either name. No check, nobody reacts, gone under the noise as fast as it arrived.

Lead with the noise. Everything today has been a queue, a counter or an office, and this is the first room that is bigger than the party rather than narrower.
beats.readAloud:
Four hundred people eating in a room built for it. It does not register as sound at all -- it registers as weather.

Every table is somebody's. You can tell by how people sit down at them -- no looking, no deciding, straight in.

Somewhere behind all of it there is a radio nobody is listening to: a man's voice, a phone-in, an argument about a harbour.

beats.text: If a player wants a real conversation with someone outside the six, offer one roll, their choice of skill.

when.condition: if a player wants to talk to someone who isn't the group or Taka

beats.note:
The scene's best chance for the table to meet the wider trainee population. Use the pilot-track and technical-track students as defaults, or invent on the spot. Never required; if nobody bites, the scene loses nothing.

CROWD-SCENE RUMOURS -- AUTHORING GAP, flagged for Ingram. The standing rule is that any crowd scene carries at least three gatherable rumours reachable by social checks, and the episode file states this scene does. It does not yet. Assembly has its three written out; this scene has raw material but no authored set. Already in the room and usable as two of the three: what Taka knows about the drains (ask-taka-directly, though that is a different, harder ask), and the pilot-track student's harbour-patrol posting as a read on the section pecking order. A third needs writing, and it should be true in substance and wrong in detail, the same as Assembly's.

beats.text: Taka arrives <trig id="taka-arrives"/> uninvited and claims all six of them as his before the plates are cleared -- dragging chairs over, making room, declaring them his table's problem now, whether they like it or not.
beats.direction:
The warmth comes from INCLUSION, not labelling. Total confidence, zero permission asked, but aimed at the group and at whatever they actually did or said a moment ago in the-room, not at inventing who each of them is.

If a player mentioned anything specific, Taka seizes on it immediately and loudly. If nobody did, he is simply, overwhelmingly glad they exist and says so. If a player pushes back in character, Taka is delighted rather than deterred.

HE DOES NOT HAND OUT NICKNAMES, AND THAT IS A LIVE DECISION RATHER THAN A RULE. Having him name each of them would need the GM to characterise six unknown PCs correctly, live, in a beat that then sticks for the rest of the campaign, and that is too precise a guess to make before the six real PCs exist. It is a genuinely good beat for a character somebody already knows -- worth revisiting once there is something real to react to.

He does not introduce himself and he does not ask. The warmth is in the assumption that of course he is sitting here.

**Aim everything he says at what the party actually did or said a moment ago**, never at inventing who any of them is.
beats.note: ask-taka becomes available once he is actually in the scene -- see the check beat below.
beats.readAloud:
A chair arrives before its owner does. <trig id="taka-arrives"/> Then another one.

"Right -- budge up. No, properly budge up, there's six of you and I can't sit on the end like a coat."

Nobody asked him. Nobody is going to.

beats.text: If a player asks Taka directly and specifically what the storm drain job is actually like, offer the check.

when.condition: if a player asks Taka directly, not just generally, about the assignment

beats.note: One of the two 'verbal investigation' paths. He won't volunteer this -- it has to be a real, specific question.

beats.text: If a player wants to think about what they actually know about storm drains near the harbour, offer the check.

when.condition: if a player wants to try recalling something relevant, at any point in the scene

beats.note: The hard Recall Knowledge path. Never required, costs nothing on any result -- an Encyclopaedia check.

beats.text: The Section Officer comes in near the end of the meal <trig id="section-officer-arrives"/> with a clipboard, waits for the room to notice him, and reads the evening's section assignments out himself. Several other sections get theirs first. Section Nine's is last.
beats.readAloud:
"Section Four, harbour patrol, report to the east gate." He doesn't look up between entries. "Section Six, assist Structural with a survey, Hangar Two."

A pause. He looks up for this one. "Section Nine: storm drain clearance, access via Dock C.

Report by nineteen-hundred. Bring waders."
beats.direction:
No choice is offered and none should seem available -- this isn't a negotiation. If a player objects or asks for a different assignment, the answer is procedural and final: reassignments aren't handled in a canteen, take it up through your section, next. The other sections' better-sounding jobs are the point. He does not gloat in words, and he does not have to -- he came down here to read this out himself when he could have sent it, and he looks up for exactly one entry on the list.

THE READ-ALOUD IS DROPPABLE UNITS. Cut from the middle if the table is ahead of it; keep the first and the last.

NOBODY HAS TO ROLL HERE EITHER. A player who sits through the announcement and says nothing has done a normal thing. The check is for somebody who reacts.
beats.note:
He is a face in the room rather than a voice on a tannoy, which is what makes read-the-announcement worth rolling -- reading a man is more interesting than reading a loudspeaker.

GM-ONLY: same man as Kit Issue and The Errand, same grudge, no second more deliberate hand behind it. If a critical success asks who did this on purpose, the honest answer is one petty, familiar man standing right there, not an institution with a plan for them.

outro.endsWhen: The moment the assignment lands. Don't let the scene wander after it -- end on the deflation, the same way Intake Medicals ended on the all-six realisation.

tracks.why: The room got bigger and louder tonight, and Section Nine ended it with a shared, specific grievance: the worst job on the list, read last and read flat, after everyone else's sounded better. A pecking order they can resent together is exactly what turns six strangers into a section.

transition.line: He already said it, to their faces: storm drain clearance, access via Dock C, report by nineteen-hundred. No choice was offered and none should seem available now either.

outro.onwards: Kit up and walk down to Dock C first (episode-c1e1--the-walk-down, the relax beat before the fight), then into the storm drains and whatever is waiting in them.
writeDown: What Taka actually seized on or said to the table -- worth a callback later even without a fixed nickname attached to it.
Who they met outside the six, if anyone -- a real seed for Bonds later.
Who investigated the assignment and what they actually learned, since it changes how informed the party is walking into the fight -- but never changes the fight itself.

temptations.text: If nobody's tried recalling anything about storm drains near the harbour yet, that's a free Encyclopaedia check sitting right there -- worth offering to whoever seems to be thinking about it?

reactionPrompts.text: Taka's uninvited, total-confidence claiming of the table landing as warmth rather than overbearing.
The canteen actually feeling like a bigger, louder world than the day's small administrative scenes.
The flat, final "storm drain clearance, no choice offered" announcement landing as a real deflation.
reactionPrompts.scaleNote: 0 = the table shrugged it off, 10 = the mood in the room genuinely dropped.

reactionPrompts.text: Whether anyone had a real conversation with someone outside the six -- a seed for Bonds later.
Whether anyone tried to find out what's actually down in the drains before he read the assignment out and made it moot.

notes:
A two-aspect scene by design: Taka's warmth is the joke half, the cold no-choice assignment is the plant half -- the same structural rhythm as Kit Issue's Nobu / extra-thing pairing. Taka's full voice is locked in bible/characters/taka.md; read it before editing this scene.

THE PILOT-TRACK STUDENT IS A REAL, TRACKED CHARACTER (data/npcs/the-young-one.json, dossier-cicada.md #9), not flexible texture -- though nothing about how he is played tonight changes. The technical-track student remains genuinely flexible texture unless and until he is reused enough to warrant the same treatment.

WHO WROTE THE ASSIGNMENT LIST: the same Section Officer who sent them on The Errand's fool's errand. Same grudge, continuous, not a second antagonist (bible/characters/the-section-officer.md).
